newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA WHEAT BUY PRICES FALL, STILL NO DEALS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA WHEAT BUY PRICES FALL, STILL NO DEALS.

text.p: Bulgaria's Sofia Commodity Exchange (SCE) said on Friday wheat buy prices fell but sellers still considered them low and were reluctant to trade on this week's session.

"Buyers bid for 1,500 tonnes of wheat at 231,000 levs ($128.7) per tonne ex-works, but sellers refused to negotiate at these levels and no deals were struck," SCE deputy chairman Hristo Milenkov told a news conference.
Buyers bid for 1,590 tonnes last week at $135 but no deals were struck as sellers were not willing to sell below $140 per tonne ex-works.

"Bulgarian producers are hoping to sell their wheat at around $150 ex-works but anything above today's buyers' bids which are, just above the minimum farm gate price set by the cabinet, seems unrealistic at the moment," Milenkov said.

The government set the minimum farm gate price last month at 230 marks per tonne of wheat from this year's crop in a move to secure the country's grains ballance after excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year created acute grain shortages earlier this year.

"Bulgarian producers may miss a good chance to sell their wheat at a high price because wheat ex-works prices in neighbouring Romania are around $90-95 and the market can be easily flooded with cheap Romanian wheat," Milenkov said.

Bulgaria's Agriculture ministry said earlier this week the country had harvested 693,540 tonnes of wheat from 17.2 percent of the sown area so far producing an average yield of 3.27 tonnes per hectare, higher then previously estimated two tonnes per hectare.

At this yield Bulgaria may collect 3.998 million tonnes of wheat from a total of 1.225 million hectares of wheat sown area. But the farm ministry declined to make forecasts saying that a lot depended on the weather.
The country's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under futures contracts agreed earlier this year to offset bread shortages.
